newsitem.title: DUBAI: Emirates says cargo recovers from 96 yield erosion.
newsitem.headline: Emirates says cargo recovers from 96 yield erosion.

text.p: Dubai-owned Emirates airline said by the end of the financial year to March 31, 1997 its cargo division had almost completely recovered from steep yield erosion industry-wide in 1996.

"By the end of the 1996/7 financial year recovery had been almost complete from the yield erosion which hit the industry during 1996 when yields generally went into an uncontrollable nose dive," it said in a statement.

"Worldwide, we almost reached our initial targets for the financial year and exceeded our revised ones. We ended the year having achieved a 20 percent increase in revenue terms and a 23 percent increase in tonnage compared with the previous financial year," cargo senior general manager Ram Menen said.
Emirates said the Asia-Pacific region was the hardest hit in the period with yield erosion to Hong Kong at one stage almost 32 percent.
"Business is almost back to normal out of Hong Kong and in fact, that station ended the year as the region's highest contributor," the statement said.

Emirates said the European and North American region were strong and achieved 20 percent growth in uplifted tonnages in the year to end-March 1997. It said there was also increased Europe-Asia Pacific traffic.
In the region covering the Middle East, Africa and Commonwealth of Independent States, Emirates cargo revenues rose 13 percent and tonnages uplifted rose 15 percent.
The statement said Emirates has plans for expansion in Africa, but it did not elaborate.
It said cargo contributes 17.1 percent to Emirates gross revenues.
